According to DharmaNexus, the text shares 375 text-reuse passages across 40 Pali canonical and post-canonical works [DharmaNexus]. Internally, its primary reuse partners within the *Kathāvatthu* include the *Adhigayhamanasikārakathā* (Kv 16.4), *Ariyantikathā* (Kv 3.2), and *Sabbamatthītikathā* (Kv 1.6), as well as the *Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. It also exhibits significant phraseological reuse with standard canonical discourses treating the knowledge of karma and rebirth, including the *Mahāsīhanāda Sutta* (MN 12), *Sāmaññaphala Sutta* (DN 2), *Sampasādanīya Sutta* (DN 28), and sections of the Aṅguttara Nikāya (AN 3, AN 10), the *Tikapuggalapaññatti* (Pp 2.3), and the *Ñāṇakathā* of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* (Ps 1.1) [DharmaNexus]. Outside Pali, DharmaNexus automatically aligns passages of Kv 3.9 with Sanskrit works such as Harivarman's *Satyasiddhiśāstra*, the *Lalitavistara*, and the *Saṅghabhedavastu*, as well as Tibetan translations including the *Madhyamakāvatārabhāṣya* (D3862) and the *Abhiniṣkramaṇasūtra* (D0301) [DharmaNexus].
